question: An office gives visitors a badge at the front desk. The server room door opens for any badge. What is wrong?
options: The server room door should check whether this badge is allowed in that room
The front desk should check IDs more slowly
Visitors should get badges with a nicer design
The building should have more front desks
explanation: The front desk checks who you are (authentication), but each door must still check whether you may enter (authorization). A door that accepts any badge lets every visitor into the server room, just as an API that checks only "logged in" lets every user read every order.
